standard.title: Apply grammar and punctuation to compose texts
standard.description: use knowledge of modelled grammatical structures and formulaic expressions to compose and respond to texts, using appropriate punctuation and textual conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students recognise and use agreement patterns, verb forms, prepositions, adverbs and conjunctions (AC9LS4U02). They apply familiar grammatical structures in modelled contexts. They have not yet used past tense in composition, near-future structures, frequency adverbs, comparatives or consolidated agreement across complex word groups.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply modelled grammatical structures to compose and respond to texts — including tense variation, comparatives, frequency adverbs, expanded connectors and consolidated agreement patterns.

nodes.label: Tense variation and key verb structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use present, past and near-future tense in composition — selecting the appropriate tense for temporal meaning — and apply key verb distinctions with awareness.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose sentences in at least two different tenses; use a near-future structure correctly; use at least one key verb distinction in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Use present, past and near-future structures in composition; use modal expressions for hypothetical or polite statements; apply key verb distinctions in the target language; apply verb forms for self and others; apply subject pronoun conventions.
wider: Write a narrative spanning past, present and future — using each tense for its correct temporal purpose and explaining the logic of the choices
Produce paired sentences demonstrating a key verb distinction — explaining the meaning difference each produces
nodes.hinge_reason: Tense variation is the grammatical prerequisite for all narrative and temporal text production. Students who only use present tense cannot produce recounts, diary entries or future plans — core text types from this band onwards.

response_modes.reason: Tense accuracy requires repeated production practice across varied temporal contexts. Students who understand tense conceptually still default to present tense under production pressure.

success_criteria: Produces sentences in at least two different tenses correctly in a composition context
Uses a near-future structure correctly in at least one example

nodes.label: Agreement consolidation and comparatives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply agreement patterns consistently across complex word groups and use comparative structures to make comparisons.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce three word groups with correct agreement patterns; use at least one comparative structure correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Consolidate agreement patterns in complex word groups; use comparative structures for making comparisons; use ordinal expressions; use a range of connectors including contrast and reason; use location expressions for giving directions.
wider: Write a text comparing two target language communities using at least four different comparative structures
Produce a word group using the same describing word in all available agreement forms — demonstrating full agreement command

response_modes.reason: Agreement consolidation and comparative range develops through applying these structures across varied topics and text types. Varied production builds transferable accuracy rather than context-specific competence.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparative structures are where students begin to produce target language that sounds genuinely sophisticated — moving beyond basic description to evaluative and comparative expression. Width investment here produces a qualitative step up in expressive range.
success_criteria: Produces three word groups with correct agreement patterns in a composition task
Uses at least one comparative structure correctly

nodes.label: Frequency adverbs, expanded connectors and conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use frequency adverbs with flexible word order, an expanded range of connectors, and apply appropriate punctuation and textual conventions in composition.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two frequency adverbs correctly; use at least two connectors beyond the most basic; apply target language punctuation and capitalisation conventions.
nodes.typical_width: Use frequency adverbs with flexible word order; use expanded connectors including reason, contrast and addition; apply punctuation and capitalisation conventions of the target language; use number expressions for ordering and quantities; link ideas across sentences using varied connectors.
wider: Write a paragraph using at least five different connectors — demonstrating range across additive, contrastive, causal and temporal types
Revise a simple text by adding frequency adverbs and expanded connectors — compare before and after, explaining how each addition changes precision

response_modes.reason: Connector and adverb range develops through producing varied text types. Different text purposes draw on different connector types — narrative, argument and description each require different connective resources.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Expanded connectors and frequency adverbs are what move target language writing from a list of sentences to genuinely cohesive text. Width investment here produces visible quality improvement in written output.
success_criteria: Uses at least two frequency adverbs correctly with appropriate word order
Uses at least two connectors beyond the most basic in connected sentences
